correctness.rationale: The exact infection-intensity budget uses total infectious person-time E T_M to establish (1−R)E T_M=1−(R/M)J_M, J_M=E∫Σ_ij P_ij I_i C_j dt. A same-seed subcritical multitype birth-death process dominates SIR, has finite second moments, and finite genealogy collision probability O(1/M); integrated quadratic moments provide an integrable dominating variable so J_M→J∞. With D=I−RP, m′=−Dm, Y′=−DY−YD+diag((I+RP)m), X′=−DX+RYP+Rdiag(Pm). Symmetry/stochasticity and uniform seed solve ∫Y=D⁻¹/[n(1−R)] and ∫X=D⁻²/[n(1−R)]. Thus J∞=tr(PD⁻²)/[n(1−R)] and the coefficient follows. Neumann series K=[n(1−R)²]⁻¹ Σ_{k≥1} kR^k tr(P^k) positive (trace P²>0 if trace P=0). For Q symmetric stochastic, f′_R(x)=(1+Rx)/(1−Rx)³>0 on [-1,1], so K increases with identity-mixing θ. Independent exact-rational dynamic programming on finite SIR states, resolvent and integrated-moment matrix checks corroborate two-patch and one-patch examples without replacing the analytic coupling proof.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and do not replace the analytical all-parameter proof.

final_claim: For fixed symmetric nonnegative row-stochastic n×n patch mixing P and 0<R<1, a uniformly seeded continuous-time Markov SIR epidemic with M people per patch satisfies E T_M=1/(1−R)−[R/(n(1−R)²M)] tr[P(I−RP)⁻²]+o(1/M). The positive correction has nonnegative closed-walk expansion and increases strictly along P_θ=θI+(1−θ)Q for any Q≠I of this class.
